title: Note The Difference Between The 1st Chapter And The 2nd Chapter

questions.question: Why does the traveler begin a new journey with his intellect?
questions.answer: He wants to look for clear signs that show Allah is One.

questions.question: Where do the traveler and his intellect stop first?
questions.answer: They arrive at the first stopping-place in their new search.

questions.question: What do they see at that first stopping-place?
questions.answer: They see four holy and clear truths spread across the whole universe.

questions.question: What do those four truths prove?
questions.answer: They prove the unity of Allah.

questions.question: In this passage, what was the traveler’s earlier goal in being sent to the world?
questions.answer: It was to reach faith.

questions.question: How had the traveler searched before this new journey?
questions.answer: He had traveled through the universe in his mind, asking creation about its Creator.

questions.question: What level of certainty had the traveler already reached before starting this new journey?
questions.answer: He had reached certainty about the Necessary Existence of his Creator.

questions.question: What does the phrase about the truths “prevailing over the whole cosmos” suggest?
questions.answer: It suggests that these signs are universal, not limited to one place or one group of things.

questions.question: What can we infer about the role of the intellect in this passage?
questions.answer: The intellect is being used as a companion in thinking, reflecting, and recognizing the proofs.

questions.question: Which is the main theme of this short passage: Allah’s forgiveness, the history of prophets, or proofs of Allah’s unity?
questions.answer: Proofs of Allah’s unity.

questions.question: Who is the main person described in the passage?
questions.answer: A traveler seeking true faith and certainty about Allah.

questions.question: What had this traveler been asking throughout the universe?
questions.answer: He had been asking everything about its Maker.

questions.question: What was he trying to find in every place?
questions.answer: He was trying to find his Lord, Allah.

questions.question: After reaching certainty about Necessary Existence, what new goal does he choose?
questions.answer: He chooses to search for proofs that Allah is One.

questions.question: Whom does the traveler speak to before beginning the new journey?
questions.answer: He speaks to his intellect.

questions.question: How many sacred truths are seen at the first stopping-place?
questions.answer: Four.

questions.question: How are those truths described in relation to the cosmos?
questions.answer: They are described as ruling or appearing over the whole universe.

questions.question: What kind of proof do these truths give about Allah’s unity?
questions.answer: They give proof that is obvious and strong.

questions.question: Why is the first stopping-place important in the passage?
questions.answer: It begins the next part of the traveler’s search by showing broad signs of tawhid.

questions.question: What title is given to this section of the passage?
questions.answer: It is about proofs of Divine unity.

questions.question: Why is the traveler described as someone sent to the world to attain faith?
questions.answer: It shows that faith is a major purpose of his life and journey.

questions.question: What method did the traveler use to explore the cosmos?
questions.answer: He traveled through it in his mind.

questions.question: What had the traveler already found with complete certainty before this part begins?
questions.answer: He had found certainty that the Creator necessarily exists.

questions.question: What did he still want to understand more clearly?
questions.answer: He wanted to see the proofs that this Creator is One.

questions.question: Why does the traveler invite his intellect to come along?
questions.answer: Because understanding Allah’s signs requires thought and reflection.

questions.question: What happens when they reach the first stopping-place?
questions.answer: They observe four sacred truths present throughout the universe.

questions.question: What does it mean that these truths “necessitated” Allah’s unity?
questions.answer: It means these truths strongly require the conclusion that Allah is One.

questions.question: Write the main idea of the passage in one sentence.
questions.answer: A traveler who already knows Allah exists begins a new search, using the intellect to see universal proofs that Allah is One.

questions.question: Before the new journey starts, what has the traveler already been doing?
questions.answer: He has been searching across the universe for knowledge of his Creator.

questions.question: In what way did he travel through the whole cosmos?
questions.answer: He did so in his mind.

questions.question: What does this mental journey tell us about the kind of search being described?
questions.answer: It is a search through reflection, understanding, and signs, not just physical movement.

questions.question: What was the traveler seeking in every place?
questions.answer: He was seeking his Sustainer and trying to find Allah.

questions.question: What certainty had he reached at the point mentioned in the passage?
questions.answer: He had reached certainty about the Necessary Existence of the Creator.

questions.question: What does the traveler ask his intellect to do next?
questions.answer: He tells it to come on a new journey.

questions.question: What is the purpose of this new journey?
questions.answer: To witness the proofs that the Creator is One.

questions.question: Who goes on this journey together?
questions.answer: The traveler and his intellect.

questions.question: What do they witness at the first stopping-place?
questions.answer: They witness four sacred truths spread over the whole cosmos.

questions.question: How clear are these truths said to be?
questions.answer: They are described as plainly showing the unity of Allah.

questions.question: Why is the whole cosmos mentioned instead of one small part of creation?
questions.answer: Because the proof being presented is broad, universal, and found everywhere.

questions.question: What is the traveler ultimately trying to gain through his search?
questions.answer: Firm faith and certain knowledge of Allah.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the traveler’s search across creation?
questions.answer: It describes him as mentally journeying through the universe and asking everything about its Maker.

questions.question: What had he already become certain of before the second chapter begins?
questions.answer: He had become certain that the Creator necessarily exists.

questions.question: What question is the new journey trying to answer?
questions.answer: It is trying to show that the Creator is One.

questions.question: Why is the intellect addressed directly in the passage?
questions.answer: To show that the mind should actively help in recognizing truth.

questions.question: At the first stopping-place, how many major truths appear?
questions.answer: Four major truths appear.

questions.question: Are those truths limited to a single area of life?
questions.answer: No, they cover the whole cosmos.

questions.question: What is one main difference between the traveler’s earlier search and his new journey?
questions.answer: Earlier he was seeking certainty that the Creator exists; now he is seeking proofs of Allah’s unity.

questions.question: What subject does this chapter focus on?
questions.answer: It focuses on the proofs that Allah is One.

questions.question: Who is the traveler described in the passage?
questions.answer: He is a person seeking faith by reflecting on the universe.

questions.question: Why did the traveler examine the whole cosmos in his mind?
questions.answer: He wanted to ask creation about its Creator and find his Sustainer.

questions.question: What had he found with the greatest certainty before this new stage?
questions.answer: He had found certainty that his Creator necessarily exists.

questions.question: What does he say to his intellect?
questions.answer: He invites it to join a new journey.

questions.question: What is the aim of that journey?
questions.answer: To witness the evidences of the Creator’s unity.

questions.question: What does this tell us about the place of the intellect in faith?
questions.answer: The intellect is a useful tool for understanding and confirming belief.

questions.question: Where do they go first in this stage of the journey?
questions.answer: They go to the first stopping-place.

questions.question: What do they see there?
questions.answer: They see four sacred truths active across the universe.

questions.question: What do these truths make clear?
questions.answer: They make clear that Allah’s unity is certain.

questions.question: What is the best summary of the passage?
questions.answer: A seeker who already knows Allah exists begins a new stage of reflection with his intellect and finds universal truths pointing to Allah’s oneness.
